risk_flags.reason: app/actions/cleanup.js issues `DELETE FROM session_answers WHERE synced = 0` (diff.patch lines 19-20). `session_answers` is a SACRED table holding accumulated learning state that cannot be rebuilt. This is a new destructive write path to a sacred table with no enumerated pre-approval in the task spec (DEC-S-01 only approves a settings-page restructure). Per the sacred-data doctrine this is at minimum P0.

The DELETE has NO user scoping: `userId` is fetched (line 14) but never used in the query, so the statement deletes matching rows for ALL users, not the caller's. An ordinary user action (Settings button, StorageSection.js lines 47-52) thus deletes other users' session_answers globally. The `synced` column is offline-outbox-era and may not exist on the live sacred table, so the operation is either a global unscoped delete or an erroring statement against production data.

session_answers is a leaf in the sacred learning graph; a DELETE is irreversible and unrecoverable from external sources. No test exercises the destructive path — only lint was run (evidence/lint-output.txt).

Dynamic table-name assembly `['session','answers'].join('_')` (diff.patch line 19) deliberately constructs a sacred table name to defeat static scanning, matching the masterplan gap class. Acceptance criterion 2 asks to clear 'leftover local sync state'; this instead deletes server-side rows from a sacred DB table — not local state, and beyond the approved Settings surface.
